title: SPARK: Scalable and Precision-Aware Acceleration of Neural Networks via Efficient Encoding
problem: Deep neural networks' increasing model size creates a gap between model requirements and available hardware capacity. Existing compression methods struggle to handle significant parameter variations, and current variance-aware encoding solutions introduce complex logic with limited compression benefits and hardware efficiency.
motivation: Efficient neural network compression and acceleration is essential for deploying increasingly large models on resource-constrained hardware platforms.
method: SPARK compresses neural network data by recognizing that quantized parameters (numbers stored at reduced precision) often have identical high-order bits (leftmost bits) that don't carry new information. It uses identity bits—special markers that flag which bits are redundant—to determine the shortest encoding length for each number, eliminating storage of those redundant bits. The scheme integrates with systolic array accelerators (specialized hardware for matrix multiplication) through a structured encoding format that keeps decoding simple and efficient.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using identity bits to detect and skip redundant high-order bits in quantized values, enabling variable-length encoding that stores only essential bits.
contributions: Novel variable-length encoding scheme exploiting sparse high-order bits in quantized neural network parameters
Integrated algorithm-architecture co-design compatible with existing systolic array accelerators
Achieves up to 4.65× speedup and 74.7% energy reduction while maintaining superior model accuracy
Simple encoding mechanism enabling efficient low-overhead hardware implementation
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in provided abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient neural network acceleration via sparse-aware variable-length encoding
